In one scene, they successfully capture Don Emilio and his associates, using a combination of laser weaponry and stun grenades. The remaining scenes of the episode show Ador adjusting to life with his wife and son, and occasionally being checked on by SCP-3922-A instances. The episode ends with Ador and his wife guiding their son to school, as the camera pans out showing multiple SCP-3922-A instances protecting the school and other buildings nearby which are all painted with The Three Moons insignia.

Subject: A recorded playthrough of Five Nights at Freddy's, 2014, T
Interference Point: Beginning of playthrough
Result: The playthrough consists of the night guard lazily checking security footage, reading newspapers, drinking coffee, and facing no danger whatsoever. While the animatronics occasionally move, they are fully contained within experimental devices labeled "RESIDUAL ACTIVITY SUPPRESSION MATRIX V 1.20" and bearing the ☽☽☽ Psychotronics Division insignia. One of the articles in the night guard's newspapers involves the corpse of a man named William Afton being found in a ditch with 1,302 bullet wounds.

Subject: Potter Puppet Pals: The Mysterious Ticking Noise, 2007, Unrated
Interference Point: Right before Ron discovers the pipe bomb.
Result: Five SCP-3922-A instances appear as puppets, they immediately warn Ron to stay away from the pipe bomb. The SCP-3922-A instances quickly disable the bomb. Voldemort appears confused by the appearance of SCP-3922-A instances. The SCP-3922-A instances immediately kill Voldemort by using revolvers. All the puppets shout "Yay!" after Voldemort's defeat. All the puppets then slide down, then a sign appears saying "THE END -☽☽☽". The curtains slide back in.

Subject: A recorded playthrough of Hatred, 2015, AO
Interference Point: At the start of the game.
Result: The main character is immediately killed by an unseen sniper, ending the video.
Note: Title card at the end was different, reading only "NO. ☽☽☽"

Subject: The Menu, 2022, R
Interference Point: During the introduction of Sous-Chef Jeremy Louden's "The Mess"
Result: 15 instances of SCP-3922-A storm the front entrance of Hawthorne carrying assault rifles shooting Jeremy Loudin and Julian Slowik non-lethally in the legs. Carrying the rear is Doug Verrick wearing a harness with angel wings in handcuffs. The instances of SCP-3922-A enter the kitchen and procure several bowls of emulsions from the 3rd Course "Breadless Bread Plate" and shrink wrap. They proceed to use emulsions and shrink wrap to waterboard and interrogate Tyler Ledford in the middle of the restaurant while rhetorically asking "You wanted to be embalmed in this. Right?". Tyler confesses over the course of 15 minutes to his correspondence with Chef Julian Slowik, the latter's plan to kill everyone present, the specifics of why Slowik wants to kill them, and the fact that Margot is an escort. Following this, SCP-3922-A instances arrest Slowik and his staff for attempted murder as well as Bryce, Soren, and Dave for their white-collar crimes. The rest of the guests are escorted off the island to safety. Tyler is left in the restaurant. The duration of the film's runtime is dedicated to showing Tyler trapped on the island, unable to leave or call for help and struggling to use the tools and ingredients from the restaurant's kitchen.

Subject: Dining Room or There is Nothing, 2006, Unrated
Interference Point: Right before the woman's head falls into the bowl.
Result: Two SCP-3922-A instances immediately appear and prevent the woman's head from falling into the bowl of soup. They quickly attend to the woman, checking for any injuries or signs of distress. The woman initially wakes up in shock at the sudden appearance of the SCP-3922-A instances, but calms down once they reassure her and explain their purpose. They advise her to be careful.

Subject: POSSIBLY IN MICHIGAN, 1983, Unrated
Interference Point: When the cannibal first comes into the mall.
Result: The cannibal is immediately arrested by SCP-3922-A instances for stalking and attempted cannibalism. The SCP-3922-A instances then proceed to take the cannibal away, while the two young women of the video look on in shock.

Subject: Blank Room Soup.avi, 2006, Unrated
Interference Point: When one of the people wearing a RayRay costume is approaching the man.
Result: SCP-3922-A instances immediately burst into the room, shooting both RayRays. One of the SCP-3922-A instances is then seen comforting the man that was eating soup.

Subject: "Snuff Films Do Not Exist", 2000, Unrated
Interference Point: Title of the film.
Result: Immediately cuts to an end title, reading "AND YOU CAN HELP MAKE THAT A REALITY, CITIZEN! ☽☽☽"

Subject: LACKADAISY (Pilot), 2023, Unrated
Interference Point: 5:51 into the video, When the Lackadaisy trio30 are Ambushed by the Marigold Gang.
Result: As Ivy turns around, an SCP-3922-A instance steps out of the vehicle, carrying a Browning Automatic Fire, before opening fire. The video continues as normal (aside from the lack of the Marigold Gang) until 15:52 in the video, when one of the SCP-3922-A instances says, supposedly to a superior, “We lost them, we’ll try again later.” The episode continues as normal, except for the post credit scene, which is removed entirely.
Note: Usually, SCP-3922-A would’ve taken care of them by the first chance, but it’s almost like they were purposefully going easy on the Lackadaisy Crew. But that begs the question, what makes Lackadaisy so different from any other sort of media they’ve encountered before? Surely, given the legality of prohibition at the time, they would have gone much harder on them, right? Perhaps more indie media needs to be tested in the near future. - Dr. Nasimith

Subject: Robots, 2005, PG
Interference Point: When Bigweld knocks over the dominoes on The Bigweld Show.
Result: As the dominoes knock over, they land on the pause button of a remote control that resembles SCP-5510. Bigweld and the various object and characters in the background freeze in place. 15 seconds later, Bigweld's body opens up to reveal a CGI render resembling a
simulacrum of Mel Brooks circa 2005 wearing a blue motion capture suit. The following exchange ensues.

Brooks: Alright, come on out! I know you guys are hiding here.
Several automatons resembling anthropomorphic instances of SCP-2578 wearing SCP-3922-A attire materialize around Mel Brooks.
Brooks: I knew it! I thought I was clear about this: You guys are not supposed to interfere with my movies.
Brooks points directly to the screen.
Brooks: And you guys are not supposed to run experiments on my movies.
One of the automatons opens up to reveal a CGI render of SCP-3922-A, wearing a white motion capture suit.
SCP-3922-A: Mr. Brooks, with all due respect, this is not your movie. You didn't direct or pro…
Brooks: You think I don't know that! That's why I got this!
Brooks produces a clipboard containing several sheets of paper from the Bigweld exoskeleton and hands it to the SCP-3922-A instance. They proceed to thumb through the sheets for 5 minutes.
SCP-3922-A: Yeah, okay, fantastic.
Instance directly faces the camera
SCP-3922-A: So um, just so you guys at home know, this is an amendment to the Melvin James Kaminsky Exclusion Act of 1945 ratified in 2015. The TL;DR is that it extends the legal definition of a Mel Brooks movie to anything that he was even remotely involved in the creation of. This includes movies that Mel Brooks produced, wrote for, directed, or starred in. It also extends this exemption to any movie that starred an actor whose career was heavily dependent on Brooks, like Gene Wilder.
The SCP-3922-A holds up the document to the screen which contains the signatures of all current, past, and future members the O-5 Council, The Ethics Committee, the Administrator, and Dr. Naismith31. He proceeds to hand it back to Brooks.
Brooks: Thank you! Now get out of here.
SCP-3922-A instances climb back inside their exoskeletons and promptly de-manifest. Mel Brooks places a domino into Bigweld's right hand. He climbs back into Bigweld with the SCP-5510 replica. He pauses to look back at the screen.
Brooks: Honestly, I think you guys have bigger fish to fry than shoehorning the space men into your favorite movies. Don'tcha think?
Bigweld closes. The film resumes with no further alterations.

Note: … No seriously, how? I don't even remember signing that thing.- Dr. Naismith

Subject: Who Killed Captain Alex?, 1 March 2010
Interference Point: End of film
Result: In an end credits scene, a single SCP-3922-A instance is sitting in a chair. They turn to the camera and say, "What was that?"
Note: Sounds about right. - Researcher Lang

Subject: Chainsaw Man, Episode 1 "Dog & Chainsaw", 2022, TV-MA
Interference Point: The Zombie Devil reveals itself and sends its zombies to kill Denji and Pochita.
Result: Multiple SCP-3922-A instances storm the warehouse and gun down the zombies and the Zombie Devil itself. One of the instances then approaches Denji and offers him food and shelter. However, the instance then suddenly undergoes a drastic change in personality, exclaiming to Denji that "the boss" is here. As in the unaltered episode, Makima arrives in a car with her assistants, except the three of them are wearing ID badges in Japanese emblazoned with ☽☽☽ symbols. All instances of SCP-3922-A immediately begin praising Makima. Makima approaches Denji, and politely asks him for Pochita so they can take care of him together. Denji, infatuated with her, obliges as Pochita begins to growl and snarl at Makima. Makima faces the camera and [DATA EXPUNGED], necessitating that all researchers present be administered Class A amnestics.
Note: Proposal to require extensive research of the source material before further testing of SCP-3922. Researcher Kwon hadn't read the manga and was unaware of Makima's true nature and power level, and because of her ignorance we nearly got a new dangerous anomaly running loose. - Dr. Hawthorne

Subject: Borat! Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan, 2006, R
Interference Point: The scene where Borat Sagdiyev is chasing an American civilian with the stated aim of "saying hi".
Result: Several SCP-3922-A instances interfere to restrain Borat and place him in a black truck which carries the ☽☽☽ symbol on it. They then take him into a rehabilitation clinic where numerous citizens of other Third World nations are schooled in classes taught by SCP-3922-A instances. The rest of the movie consists of SCP-3922-A's semi-successful attempts to teach Borat about Western culture and human decency, however, Borat's ignorancy and obliviousness make this process extremely difficult. The movie lasts for close to 2 hours 45 minutes, and in the end, Borat is deemed "safe for the public" and is reintegrated into American society.

Subject: Salad Fingers, Episode 1 “Spoons”, 2004, Unrated
Interference Point: Entire episode.
Result: Instances of SCP-3922-A deploy via dropship and proceed to apprehend Salad Fingers and admit him into a mental asylum. The rest of the episode consists of the titular character recovering from his mental state through methods such as psychological therapy with an instance of SCP-3922-A medical personnel, usage of a medication labelled as “Tactical Anti-Hallucinogenics”, peer support involving multiple SCP-3922-A instances, with a significant change in the appearance of the episode to display the main character’s rehabilitation and his severe hallucinations recovering as a result. By the end of the episode, Salad Fingers is displayed as an ordinary human being working at an office building, fully integrated into society. The episode’s credits are preceded by the Three Moons title card accompanied by the words, “Mental stability is of utmost importance.”
Note: There goes my childhood nightmares. -Dr. Suzuki

Subject: “Learning With Pibby” Official Trailer
Interference Point: None, test canceled
Result: None, test canceled
Note: There is no telling how SCP-3922-A would react to this. What if it gets consumed, or even worse, spreads? — Dr. Une

Subject: The remake of the music video for the song "Freestyler", by Bomfunk MC's, 2019, not rated.
Interference point: Immediately after Raymond Ebanks ("B.O. Dubb") imbues the protagonist's mobile phone with reality-altering capabilities.
Result: The other passengers in the subway car have been replaced by five instances of SCP-3922-A. One instance confiscates the mobile phone, while the other four confront Dubb, accusing him of being dangerously irresponsible. Accompanied by a techno/hip-hop beat,32 Dubb responds that he did nothing wrong, points out that the protagonist's reality-altering activities would have been carefully monitored, emphasizes that he was prepared to completely rewind time and undo the events if the protagonist began to abuse her newfound abilities, and says "The best way to test a potential recruit's moral fitness is to let them think they have unlimited power. " During this, the protagonist appears significantly distressed. The instances quietly discuss Dubb's points among themselves, then offer the mobile phone to the protagonist. Instead of taking it, she recoils in horror and flees, jumping out of the subway car and onto the platform; the camera then shows her running up the escalator and out of the subway station.
Investigation of Ebanks and the other members of Bomfunk MC's has not revealed any anomalous phenomena.

Subject: A Serbian Film (2010)
Interference Point: Beginning of the film
Result: Entire film is replaced with Don Bluth's A Troll in Central Park (1994) with Serbian subtitles.
Note: Well, it's a Serbian film now. - Researcher Paulsen

Subject: Found (2012), Unrated (Rated 18 in the United Kingdom)
Interference point: The scene after Marcus bullies Marty
Result: Marty is approached by an unarmed instance of SCP-3922-A when nobody else is around, who asks him if he is okay, to which a surprised Marty enters a conversation with the strange man who acts as a sort of personal therapist to him, to which he eventually gets Marty, who is feeling scared and uneasy, to confess about Steve’s activities, just wanting for all the pain and bullying to stop, to which the SCP-3922-A instance after comforting him calls his superiors on a walkie talkie, confirming to them that “they’ve got the one”. Soon enough in the next scene Marty’s home is raided by several SCP-3922-A agents, with them finding Steve in his room and demanding him to get down onto ground, to which he immediately attempts to flee with his weapons but is incapacitated and taken into custody, his parents unable to do anything but watch in shock and horror, while a single 3922-A instance inspects the bowling ball bag, confirming it to his superiors over the radio that the severed head of an African American woman who recently went missing is inside, with Steve being charged with multiple murders and planning another and being hauled off to jail.

The rest of the film depicts Marty’s parents’ and the town’s reaction to his older brother being a serial killer who primarily targeted black people because of his racist views. Marty’s father is eventually arrested soon afterwards for child abuse, while him and his mother both receive psychotherapy by the Three Moons Initiative, trying to understand and come to terms with what has happened, with Marty attempting to improve his life and stand up for himself, while not embracing the evils that his brother committed.

Subject: Threads (1984), 15
Interference point: Beginning
Result: The film becomes a five-minute series of radio and news reports detailing how the Three Moons Initiative has led peace talks between the Soviet Union and the United States over the situation in Iran, with leaders of both nations agreeing to donate their entire nuclear arsenal to the Initiative "for their struggle against the Threll Dominion."

Subject: Funny Games (1997), Not Rated (16 in Austria)
Interference point: Beginning
Result: 109 uninterrupted minutes of the Schober family (including Sissi) playing humorous board games. Seen briefly through their window, the house guarded by a fortified detachment of SCP-3922-A.

Subject: The Poughkeepsie Tapes, 2007, R
Interference Point: The Beginning
Result: The intro of the movie is skipped over entirely, beginning with the first tape of Edward Carver, the serial killer of the movie, in the process of abducting his first victim, an eight-year-old girl, when he is suddenly ambushed and put under arrest by a SWAT team of SCP-3922-A, where he is taken away into a police van, the little girl being taken care of by a single 3922-A instance while the voice of who is presumably her mother rushes onto the scene, and Carver’s camera is picked up before being turned off. Most of the film’s runtime is home videos and other media of his victims from the original film, enjoying their lives without them being ended and/or ruined by Carver. At the end of the film in 2001, police raid a house in Poughkeepsie, New York, who discover Carver in the basement, rescued but being irreversibly damaged from his ordeal, having clearly been tortured and imprisoned over a very long period of time, where upon plans and evidence of his crimes and mental state being found all over his home, he is sent to a psychiatric hospital. Instead of getting to sadistically enjoy infamy as one of the most feared serial killers in the country, Edward instead ends up as an obscure case of a mentally unwell man who was punished for crimes he planned to do but ultimately wasn’t able to commit. The final scene of the movie shows teenager Cheryl Dempsey happily celebrating her birthday with her family, friends, and her boyfriend Tim.
Note: “Well, I got to say that was chilling but quite unique for the Three Moons Initiative, instead of just killing him on the spot, they let him live, but neither being able to commit any of his crimes due to the intense trauma inflicted upon him, nor will he be able to get any attention from committing such horrific acts. For all intents and purposes, he will just be a traumatized, lonely nobody.” - Researcher Lang

Subject: Saw, (2004), R
Interference Point: When Zep moves to murder Alison and Diana
Result: A SWAT van with the Three Moons Initiative’s insignia displayed on the right-side of the vehicle pulls up outside the Gordon’s residence, much to Detective Tapp’s confusion. A team of SCP-3922-A burst through the door and with the help of Alison overwhelm and arrest a scared and hopeless Zap Hindle. Alison tells Lawrence over the phone that she’s she’s alive, which prevents him from cutting off his own foot. Using the information from a defeated Zep, the 3922-A, joined by Tapp, rush over to the sewers, where they reach Lawrence and Adam, freeing them both from their chains, and upon discovering that the corpse in the middle of the room is actually still alive apprehended him and take away for questioning. The film ends with Adam, Lawrence, and the others being questioned by police and being attended by doctors, where Adam talks to the police due to his job as a photographer, Lawrence confesses having an affair to his wife where after all they have been through respectively decide to get a divorce, Zep gets the antidote to the poison in his body while accepting his arrest, and the mysterious man, who upon him awaking and being tazed due to him attempting to attack Tapp out of rage upon realising his plans were ruined and revealed to be John Kramer, the real Jigsaw Killer, is officially put under arrest by police, being charged for his various crimes, the film ending with the 3922-A exiting the room, Kramer yelling at them that this won’t be the end of his mission, before the door is closed on him.

Subject: Creep, (2014), R
Interference Point: When Josef attempts to stop Aaron from leaving
Result: A SWAT team of 3922-A soldiers burst into Josef’s house and overwhelm him, forcing him down to the ground and placing him under arrest, all the while Aaron is shocked as his camera keeps on rolling, asking what’s going on to, which the main soldier tells Aaron they’ll explain to him later and advise him to return back to his home. The next scene back at his home Aaron is being questioned by 3922-A investigators about Josef, being informed of his various crimes in the past, including how they found many recordings of his past victims in his house, much to Aaron’s shock and horror, realising that he himself was really close to being murdered by Josef. The rest of the film details Aaron’s investigation into Josef’s life and backstory, while the man himself is put on trial and sentenced to life in prison with no possibility of parole, with the loved ones of his past victims receiving reparations. The film ends with Aaron reminiscing about his time with Josef and his subsequent arrest, ending the film in a happy note saying that due to the attention the case received, he managed to find a job at a news company as a journalist.

Subject: A full playthrough of Amanda the Adventurer33 (2022)
Interference Point: At the end of the second puzzle.
Result: Alongside the VHS tape used to progress was an item resembling SCP-3922. The item was placed on the TV in the room prior to insertion of the tape, the contents of which vastly changing; Amanda is now instructing the player to assist her in escape while being pursued by three instances of 3922-A. Interestingly, Wooly34 is unseen.

Subject: Wolf Creek, 2005, R
Interference Point: When Mick Taylor gives Liz, Kristy, and Ben water that causes them to fall unconscious
Result: As the three tourists start to feel the effects of their water being tampered with, the sound of a vehicle screeching to a halt outside alerts Mick, only to be met by a team of SCP-3922-A who barge in through the front door and shoot him in the neck, before quickly approaching the shocked and horrified Liz, Kristy, and Ben, who they take outside while assuring them of their safety before they eventually pass out. Meanwhile Mick, who is still alive despite being shot in the neck, attempts to shoot back at the 3922-A instances, who proceed to beat, stab, and shoot Mick in various parts of his body for most of the film’s remaining runtime, where afterwards they drag him outside and throw him into a ditch, finally shooting him dead, leaving him to be found by a passing motorist (the same one who was shot dead by Mick in the original movie). SCP-3922-A instances then proceed to send evidence of Mick’s crimes to the Australian police, who investigate his home and find his large stock of cars and travellers' possessions, including video cameras, confirming he was a killer and sexual assaulter who was behind several mysterious disappearances in the Outback in the past. The final scene shows Liz, Kristy, and Ben in an Australian hospital, being aided to by doctors, nurses, and police, with the news of Mick Taylor’s body being found and his crimes being exposed, much to their shock, having coming so close to having become his newest victims, where afterwards they go back home. A series of title cards state that the families of victims of Mick Taylor were given full compensation, Mick’s home was fully cleaned out and eventually demolished, and that public discourse and controversy over the revelation of the murders leads to reforms and improvements of Australians law enforcement, especially when it comes to crimes that take place in the Outback. The film ends with the Swedish couple from the original film driving down the road in the Outback safely.

Subject: The Mist, 2007, R
Interference Point: Beginning of the film
Result: The film proceeds normally, with the citizens of Brighton, Maine dealing with a severe thunderstorm as David Drayton, his wife Stephanie, and their eight-year-old son Billy and the other characters deal with a rather unsupernatural storm when compared to the original movie, with no mist or lovecraftian monsters being seen. In one scene, a soldier named Jessup reveals while talking to two of his fellow soldiers in the local military base that a government project to discover other dimensions was indefinitely halted due to the intervention of a “Three Moons organisation”, who declared their experiment “too dangerous and risky” to the local residents, with the mysterious group supposedly entering into talks with the confused US government, who reportedly had never heard of the group before. The film ends with David, Stephanie, and Billy happily reuniting after the violent thunderstorm.
Note: I seriously hope that we just didn’t possibly give the ☽☽☽ Initiative access to interdimensional technology… - Dr. Naismith

Subject: Eden Lake, (2008), R
Interference Point: After the teens pull out knives on Steve and Jenny
Result: The scuffle is interrupted when a man offscreen yells at the group demanding to know what is going on, with it being revealed to be a group of SCP-3922-A with flashlights pointed at them, to which Steve, Jenny, and Brett’s friends immediately stand down upon realising they are armed, but after Bonnie runs at the soldiers, resulting in them being shot with a dart, Brett is sent into a rage and attacks the 3922-A commander, who simply punches him in the face, sending him to the ground unconscious, much to everybody’s shock. The 3922-A arrest the teens while taking in Steve and Jenny for questioning, who after a few minutes of talking with two 3922-A instances are let go and are helped in being given their stuff back. Meanwhile, Brett and his gang are interrogated by 3922-A instances about their activities, which include abuse, harassment, stealing, and attempted murder, with most of them being scared straight with the exception of Brett, who attempts to attack the 3922-A instances upon being enraged by them, being forced to the ground. Soon enough the kids are taken back into town, where the parents are all visited and informed of what their kids have been doing, much to their shock and disbelief, with Jon35 and the other parents angrily trying to refute this and go to comfort their kids and trying to fight for their innocence, only to be met with most of their kids confessing, scared and crying of being caught and facing punishment, with Brett simply staring blankly at his parents while the 3922-A instances provide proof and evidence of their kids’ activities and crimes, with him and his gang’s local reputation in the town basically being completely ruined. Eventually, the kids are all sentenced to juvenile detention alongside therapy, with varying sentences depending on their specific crimes, with Brett receiving the most severe sentence due to his psychotic behaviour. Alongside this, 3922-A instances, due to reports of juvenile delinquency and poor parenting, report to the local English government, successfully managing to start an investigation and programme in order to bring awareness to being good and responsible parents, while dissuading the youth from engaging in illegal activities, especially serious ones like abuse or murder. The film ends with Steve and Jenny returning home, relieved and happy to have been saved just in time before things escalated to the point that something truly terrible happened, intercut with Brett sitting in his cell.

**Subject:** //The Lion King//, 1994, G

**Interference Point:** Shortly before the stampede sequence in which Mufasa dies

**Result:** Film proceeds as normal, save for the end credits including a note after the "Special Thanks" section: "THIS NARRATIVE HAS BEEN FULLY INSPECTED BY ☽☽☽ AND WE ARE HAPPY TO REPORT THAT NO ILLEGAL HUNTING OF AFRICAN WILDLIFE HAS BEEN DETECTED."

**Note:** It is currently believed that societies that have no interactions with humanity are outside of SCP-3922-A jurisdiction.

**Subject:** CCTV recording of a 24-year-old man smoking a marijuana cigar ("blunt") outside of his Sacramento, California apartment on 9 Feb 2018.[[footnote]]To meet SCP-3922's criteria for fiction as established in the "Smokes McGee" test, a fictional narration for the footage and a false name ("Adrian Smith") for the individual were used.[[/footnote]] At the time of the footage and at time of testing, consumption of recreational marijuana was legal in the state of California but was illegal under federal law as per the Controlled Substances Act of 1970.

**Interference Point:** After the man finishes smoking and puts out the marijuana cigar by pressing it against the concrete. 

**Result:** A single SCP-3922-A instance armed with an M16 rifle approaches the man, addressing him as "Mr. Smith." After the man expresses alarm, the instance explains that it is only there to inform the man that smoking marijuana is a violation of federal law and to dispose of his cigar in the nearby dumpster. When the man replies that consumption is legal under state law, the instance hands him a small piece of paper and explains that the Three Moons Initiative is currently "conflicted as to what action to take in this circumstance" and that he will not face legal consequences as a result. The instance then reminds the man that littering is illegal under California law and to always dispose of his discarded smoking materials in proper trash receptacles after extinguishing them before walking away. 

**Note:** Conflicting laws appear to produce an uncertain and/or confused response from SCP-3922-A.

**Interference Point:** After Jimmy McGill (Saul Goodman) and Tuco Salamanca shake hands in agreement on the skateboarding twins' punishment for insulting Tuco's grandmother. 

**Result:** Before Tuco has a chance to break the twins' legs, a helicopter similar to the one seen in the previous //Breaking Bad// test approaches the scene. Tuco is executed via a long-range sniper rifle shot to the head; No-Doze and Gonzo are killed and Nacho is seriously injured as they return fire. After the helicopter touches down, an SCP-3922-A instance begins treating Nacho for his gunshot wounds while other instances interrogate Jimmy and the skateboarders. Although initially planning to arrest all three of them for "financially motivated confidence scams," Jimmy successfully persuades the 3922-A instances to not take any action, arguing that he saved the twins from a worse punishment from Tuco and that they are "so scared of you that they won't even think about jaywalking for the rest of their lives". **Interference Point:** Beginning

**Result:** As Novak prepares to leave his home on the morning of the incident, he is intercepted by five armed instances of SCP-3922-A, who confiscate his car keys and explain that his friends and relatives are concerned about his health and safety. The instances lead Novak through a series of field neurological tests, at the end of which a weeping Novak concedes that his ability to process visual input is no longer sufficient to enable him to drive safely. The instances then deliver Novak to a local hospital for diagnosis and treatment. Novak tells them that "just because you helped me doesn't mean I'm going to let you get away with anything," then promises to investigate them and expose any corruption he finds; the instances tell him that they would welcome this. A montage then depicts scenes from the next 13 months of Novak's life: unsuccessful medical procedures, reconciliations with political and professional foes, and the publication of his final column, in which he reluctantly states that he was unable to find any evidence of malfeasance from "those Three Moons bastards".

**Result:** A SWAT team of 3922-A soldiers burst into Josef’s house and overwhelm him, forcing him down to the ground and placing him under arrest, all the while Aaron is shocked as his camera keeps on rolling, asking what’s going on to, which the main soldier tells Aaron they’ll explain to him later and advise him to return back to his home. The next scene back at his home Aaron is being questioned by 3922-A investigators about Josef, being informed of his various crimes in the past, including how they found many recordings of his past victims in his house, much to Aaron’s shock and horror, realising that he himself was really close to being murdered by Josef. The rest of the film details Aaron’s investigation into Josef’s life and backstory, while the man himself is put on trial and sentenced to life in prison with no possibility of parole, with the loved ones of his past victims receiving reparations. The film ends with Aaron reminiscing about his time with Josef and his subsequent arrest, ending the film in a happy note saying that due to the attention the case received, he managed to find a job at a news company as a journalist.



**Subject:** A full playthrough of //Amanda the Adventurer//[[footnote]] A horror game in which the player must solve puzzles to uncover VHS tapes containing episodes of Amanda the Adventurer, an in-universe discontinued TV show. The main protagonist of this TV show is the antagonist of the horror game.[[/footnote]] (2022)

**Interference Point:** At the end of the second puzzle.

**Result:** Alongside the VHS tape used to progress was an item resembling SCP-3922. The item was placed on the TV in the room prior to insertion of the tape, the contents of which vastly changing; Amanda is now instructing the player to assist her in escape while being pursued by three instances of 3922-A. Interestingly, Wooly[[footnote]] The secondary protagonist of the game, his role being Amanda’s assistant. He is aware and disapproving of Amanda’s malicious intentions.[[/footnote]] is unseen.



**Subject:** //Wolf Creek//, 2005, R

**Interference Point:** When Mick Taylor gives Liz, Kristy, and Ben water that causes them to fall unconscious

**Result:** As the three tourists start to feel the effects of their water being tampered with, the sound of a vehicle screeching to a halt outside alerts Mick, only to be met by a team of SCP-3922-A who barge in through the front door and shoot him in the neck, before quickly approaching the shocked and horrified Liz, Kristy, and Ben, who they take outside while assuring them of their safety before they eventually pass out. Meanwhile Mick, who is still alive despite being shot in the neck, attempts to shoot back at the 3922-A instances, who proceed to beat, stab, and shoot Mick in various parts of his body for most of the film’s remaining runtime, where afterwards they drag him outside and throw him into a ditch, finally shooting him dead, leaving him to be found by a passing motorist (the same one who was shot dead by Mick in the original movie). SCP-3922-A instances then proceed to send evidence of Mick’s crimes to the Australian police, who investigate his home and find his large stock of cars and travellers' possessions, including video cameras, confirming he was a killer and sexual assaulter who was behind several mysterious disappearances in the Outback in the past. The final scene shows Liz, Kristy, and Ben in an Australian hospital, being aided to by doctors, nurses, and police, with the news of Mick Taylor’s body being found and his crimes being exposed, much to their shock, having coming so close to having become his newest victims, where afterwards they go back home. A series of title cards state that the families of victims of Mick Taylor were given full compensation, Mick’s home was fully cleaned out and eventually demolished, and that public discourse and controversy over the revelation of the murders leads to reforms and improvements of Australians law enforcement, especially when it comes to crimes that take place in the Outback. The film ends with the Swedish couple from the original film driving down the road in the Outback safely.



**Subject:** //The Mist//, 2007, R

**Interference Point:** Beginning of the film

**Result:** The film proceeds normally, with the citizens of Brighton, Maine dealing with a severe thunderstorm as David Drayton, his wife Stephanie, and their eight-year-old son Billy and the other characters deal with a rather unsupernatural storm when compared to the original movie, with no mist or lovecraftian monsters being seen. In one scene, a soldier named Jessup reveals while talking to two of his fellow soldiers in the local military base that a government project to discover other dimensions was indefinitely halted due to the intervention of a “Three Moons organisation”, who declared their experiment “too dangerous and risky” to the local residents, with the mysterious group supposedly entering into talks with the confused US government, who reportedly had never heard of the group before. The film ends with David, Stephanie, and Billy happily reuniting after the violent thunderstorm.

**Note:** I seriously hope that we just didn’t possibly give the ☽☽☽ Initiative access to interdimensional technology… - Dr. Naismith



**Subject:** //Eden Lake//, (2008), R

**Interference Point:** After the teens pull out knives on Steve and Jenny

**Result:** The scuffle is interrupted when a man offscreen yells at the group demanding to know what is going on, with it being revealed to be a group of SCP-3922-A with flashlights pointed at them, to which Steve, Jenny, and Brett’s friends immediately stand down upon realising they are armed, but after Bonnie runs at the soldiers, resulting in them being shot with a dart, Brett is sent into a rage and attacks the 3922-A commander, who simply punches him in the face, sending him to the ground unconscious, much to everybody’s shock. The 3922-A arrest the teens while taking in Steve and Jenny for questioning, who after a few minutes of talking with two 3922-A instances are let go and are helped in being given their stuff back. Meanwhile, Brett and his gang are interrogated by 3922-A instances about their activities, which include abuse, harassment, stealing, and attempted murder, with most of them being scared straight with the exception of Brett, who attempts to attack the 3922-A instances upon being enraged by them, being forced to the ground. Soon enough the kids are taken back into town, where the parents are all visited and informed of what their kids have been doing, much to their shock and disbelief, with Jon[[footnote]]The father of Brett.[[/footnote]] and the other parents angrily trying to refute this and go to comfort their kids and trying to fight for their innocence, only to be met with most of their kids confessing, scared and crying of being caught and facing punishment, with Brett simply staring blankly at his parents while the 3922-A instances provide proof and evidence of their kids’ activities and crimes, with him and his gang’s local reputation in the town basically being completely ruined. Eventually, the kids are all sentenced to juvenile detention alongside therapy, with varying sentences depending on their specific crimes, with Brett receiving the most severe sentence due to his psychotic behaviour. Alongside this, 3922-A instances, due to reports of juvenile delinquency and poor parenting, report to the local English government, successfully managing to start an investigation and programme in order to bring awareness to being good and responsible parents, while dissuading the youth from engaging in illegal activities, especially serious ones like abuse or murder. The film ends with Steve and Jenny returning home, relieved and happy to have been saved just in time before things escalated to the point that something truly terrible happened, intercut with Brett sitting in his cell.



------
